name: India-Pakistan confrontation (Kashmir and the post-May 2025 standoff)
summary: The ceasefire that ended four days of missile, drone and air combat in May 2025 has held for more than a year, but the two nuclear-armed rivals remain in a hostile standoff with closed airspace, mutual accusations of backing insurgents, and occasional incidents such as a collision between their warships in the Arabian Sea in September 2026.

sides.name: India
leaders: Gen. Anil Chauhan (Chief of Defence Staff)

sides.name: Pakistan
members: Pakistan Air Force (incl. No. 15 Squadron, J-10C with PL-15)

background: After militants killed tourists at Pahalgam in April 2025, India struck targets in Pakistan in Operation Sindoor and the two air forces fought a major air battle, with Pakistan crediting J-10C fighters firing PL-15 missiles with downing several Indian jets; India acknowledged losses without confirming numbers. A ceasefire took effect on 10 May 2025.

Since then the rivalry has shifted to proxies and narratives: Pakistan blames India for backing the BLA and TTP (which India denies), and India accuses Pakistan of sponsoring Kashmiri militancy. This matters because any mass-casualty attack in India attributed to a Pakistan-based group could trigger another round of cross-border strikes, now with both sides having tested each other's air defences.
year: No significant Line of Control firefights were found in sources for the window. India prosecuted the 2025 Delhi car explosion case and filed charges against Lashkar-e-Taiba founder Hafiz Saeed over the Pahalgam attack (July 2026), and designated 23 JeM and LeT operatives as terrorists on 4 July 2026. Former Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Farooq Abdullah survived an assassination attempt in Jammu on 11 March 2026. In Pakistan-administered Kashmir, clashes between police and the Joint Awami Action Committee killed 7 in Rawalakot on 7 June and 15 on 11 June 2026. Pakistan repeatedly accused India of supporting Baloch and Pakistani Taliban militants, including an October 2026 claim of Indian assistance to a militant meeting in Kandahar; India condemned Pakistan's March 2026 strike on a Kabul hospital as a 'massacre'. On 15 September 2026 a Pakistan Navy ship and an Indian Navy ship collided in the Arabian Sea, prompting protests from both sides but no casualties.
situation: As of late October 2026 the ceasefire holds and both sides keep their airspace closed to each other's aircraft. The main risks are a major militant attack in Kashmir or an Indian city, and the triangular tension created by India's growing ties with the Afghan Taliban during Pakistan's war with Kabul.
technical: May 2025 posture: India repositioned up to 20 Rafales from Hasimara and moved S-400 batteries to Adampur, Bhuj and Bikaner; mobilised about 400 aircraft; moved its Western Fleet including a carrier into the northern Arabian Sea (Wikipedia).
PAF No. 15 Squadron with J-10C and PL-15 missiles credited by PAF with the May 2025 kills (Wikipedia).

Indian losses: The Washington Quarterly assesses at least three, likely four, possibly five aircraft including at least one Rafale and a MiG-29; The Washington Post identified crash sites at Bathinda, Pampore and likely Akhnoor (Wikipedia).
Pakistan claimed to have neutralised 77 Indian drones from 6 May 2025 (Wikipedia).
Reciprocal airspace closures continued for more than a year after the ceasefire (Wikipedia).
15 Sep 2026: collision between a Pakistan Navy vessel and an Indian Navy vessel in the Arabian Sea, no casualties (Wikipedia: 2026 in India).
22 Jan 2026: an Indian Army Casspir fell into a gorge in Doda, killing 10 soldiers (accident, not hostile action) (Wikipedia: 2026 in India).
casualties: No hostile-fire deaths between Indian and Pakistani forces found for the window. Pakistan-administered Kashmir unrest killed 22 in June 2026 (Wikipedia: 2026 in Pakistan).

timeline.event: Farooq Abdullah survives assassination attempt in Jammu.
India designates 23 JeM and LeT operatives as terrorists.
Pakistani and Indian navy vessels collide in the Arabian Sea.

outlook: Watch for militant attacks in Jammu and Kashmir, rhetoric over India's ties with the Taliban, and any naval or air incidents. A repeat of Pahalgam-scale violence would likely prompt Indian strikes.
